mainTopic: Stolen ארבעה מינים: מצוה הבאה בעבירה, שמואל's first-day-only view, and buying הדסים from גוים.
overview: This עמוד explains why the משנה rules that a stolen לולב is פסול. רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, says the reason is מצוה הבאה בעבירה, a מצוה done through a sin. He learns it from a פסוק in מלאכי that groups a stolen animal with a lame one, so a stolen item stays פסול even after יאוש. The גמרא then tells a parable about a king who pays his own taxes, to show why ה׳ hates 'robbery in a burnt offering.' רבי אמי gives the same reason for a stolen לולב. שמואל disagrees and holds that a stolen לולב is פסול only on the first day, because only then must the לולב be 'לכם', your own. רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges שמואל from the משנה, and רבא defends him by reading the משנה in a 'לא מיבעיא' style. Finally, רב הונא tells הדס merchants to let the גוים cut the branches themselves, because the land may be stolen. The explanation of that advice continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A stolen item is a מצוה that comes through a sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's statement, which began on the previous עמוד, gives the reason a stolen לולב is פסול: it is a מצוה הבאה בעבירה. He brings a פסוק from מלאכי as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a מצוה that comes through a sin, as it says: 'And you have brought the stolen, and the lame, and the sick.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the reason why the משנה said a stolen לולב is פסול: you cannot do a מצוה using something you got through a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line continues רבי יוחנן's statement in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, which started on the previous עמוד. The source is a פסוק in מלאכי where the נביא rebukes the people for bringing stolen, lame, and sick animals as קרבנות. Because 'stolen' is listed next to clearly פסול animals, it is treated like them.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה that comes about through a sin
Lame (an animal with a leg blemish)
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This עמוד starts in the middle of a sentence. The speaker is רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, explaining the משנה's ruling on לולב הגזול on the previous עמוד.
steps.whyThisMatters: מצוה הבאה בעבירה is a major principle that appears all over ש״ס, not only by לולב.

phrases.english: Because it is
phrases.notes: This is the rest of what רבי יוחנן was saying on the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: a מצוה that comes through a sin,
as it is said: 'And you have brought the stolen,
and the lame, and the sick.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ מִצְוָה הַבָּאָה בַּעֲבֵירָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה's ruling on לולב הגזול (on the previous עמוד).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stolen item is פסול for a מצוה because it is a מצוה הבאה בעבירה, learned from the פסוק in מלאכי.

steps.title: Stolen is compared to lame, and neither can be fixed
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק, a stolen animal is compared to a lame one. Just as a lame animal can never be fixed, a stolen one can never be fixed, whether before or after יאוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Stolen is like lame. Just as a lame animal has no fix, so too a stolen one has no fix. It makes no difference whether it is before the owner gave up hope or after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the פסוק: 'stolen' is just like 'lame,' so it is permanently פסול. This is true even after the owner gives up hope (יאוש).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lame animal has a permanent blemish, and nothing can make it kosher for a קרבן. By grouping them together, the פסוק teaches that a stolen animal is also permanently פסול. The new point is that this applies even after יאוש, when the thief legally owns the item.

keyTerms.meaning: Despair; the owner giving up hope of getting the item back

steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase 'even after יאוש' sets up the next steps. The גמרא will show that only מצוה הבאה בעבירה can explain the case after יאוש.

phrases.english: Stolen is similar to lame:
just as a lame animal has no remedy,
so too a stolen one has no remedy,
no difference whether before despair
and no difference after despair.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּזוּל דּוּמְיָא דְּפִסֵּחַ, מָה פִּסֵּחַ לֵית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal comparison (הקש) from the פסוק quoted in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stolen animal is permanently פסול like a lame one, both before and after יאוש.

steps.title: Before the owner gives up hope, the item simply isn't the thief's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts explaining why we need the principle. Before יאוש there is an easy reason for the פסול: the קרבן must be 'yours,' and the stolen animal is not the thief's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense before the owner gives up hope: the Torah said 'when a person brings from yours,' and this animal is not his.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא grants that before יאוש there is a simple reason for the פסול, to prepare for the harder question about after יאוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'אדם כי יקריב מכם' teaches that a קרבן must belong to the person bringing it. Before יאוש the item still belongs to the original owner, so the thief cannot use it. This reason does not need מצוה הבאה בעבירה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable, granted (sets up a contrast)
From yours (the קרבן must belong to you)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא is not a conclusion. It means 'fine, this part makes sense…' and always comes before an 'אלא', meaning 'but what about…?'

phrases.english: Granted, before despair:
'When a person brings from yours'
the Merciful One said,
and it is not his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining why step 2's 'even after יאוש' requires the principle of מצוה הבאה בעבירה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before יאוש, a stolen item is פסול simply because it does not belong to the person bringing it.

steps.title: But after the owner gives up hope, the thief owns it
steps.stepSummary: After יאוש the thief legally acquires the item, so the 'not yours' reason no longer works. Why is it still פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: But after the owner gives up hope, the thief already acquired it through the despair!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: after יאוש the item does belong to the thief, so 'it isn't his' cannot be the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Halachically, a thief acquires a stolen item once the owner gives up hope. He still owes its value as a debt. So after יאוש the ownership problem from step 3 disappears, and we need a different reason for why the item is still פסול.

phrases.english: But after despair —
he already acquired it through the despair!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְאַחַר יֵאוּשׁ — הָא קַנְיֵיהּ בְּיֵאוּשׁ
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling derived in step 2 that a stolen animal is פסול even after יאוש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After יאוש the thief owns the item, so the 'מכם' (not yours) reason cannot explain why step 2 calls it פסול even after יאוש. Step 5 supplies the missing reason.

steps.title: So the reason must be מצוה הבאה בעבירה
steps.stepSummary: Since ownership cannot explain the case after יאוש, the reason must be that it is a מצוה that came through a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not because it is a מצוה that comes through a sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the only reason left for the case after יאוש is מצוה הבאה בעבירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the loop. The פסוק in מלאכי says a stolen item is always פסול, even after יאוש. Since the thief owns it by then, the only explanation is that it came through a sin. The question is rhetorical; it means 'it must be because…'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not…? (a rhetorical 'it must be')

steps.whatToRemember: Before יאוש, a stolen item is פסול because it is not yours. After יאוש, it is פסול only because of מצוה הבאה בעבירה.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not because it is
a מצוה that comes through a sin?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ מִצְוָה הַבָּאָה בַּעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem in step 4 by pointing to the principle from step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסול of a stolen item after יאוש can only be explained by מצוה הבאה בעבירה.

steps.title: A parable of a king passing a tax booth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, explains the פסוק 'I hate robbery in a burnt offering' with a parable. A king tells his servants to pay the tax at a customs house.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the פסוק mean, 'For I, ה׳, love justice; I hate robbery in a burnt offering'? It is like a human king passing a tax booth who told his servants: pay the tax to the tax collectors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אגדה, a story-lesson, that adds a moral dimension to the ban on stolen offerings. This step begins the parable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיה says ה׳ hates robbery even when it is used for a קרבן. To explain why ה׳ cares, the parable begins with a king who insists on paying tax, even though the tax ends up in his own treasury.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'For I, the Lord, love justice,
I hate robbery in a burnt offering'?
It is like a flesh-and-blood king
who was passing by a customs house.
He said to his servants:
Give the tax to the tax collectors.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching by the same speakers, adding a moral explanation to the ban on stolen offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'I hate robbery in a burnt offering' is explained through a parable of a king paying tax.

steps.title: The king explains: others will learn from me
steps.stepSummary: The servants ask why the king should pay, since all the tax is his anyway. He answers that travelers will learn from him not to dodge taxes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: doesn't all the tax belong to you? He said: all travelers will learn from me and not escape paying the tax.
steps.whatsHappening: The parable continues with the servants' question and the king's answer, which carries the main lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying tax to yourself seems pointless. The king's purpose is to set an example, so that no one feels allowed to avoid paying. The point is about teaching others, not about the money.

phrases.english: They said to him: But isn't all the tax
entirely yours?
He said to them:
From me all travelers will learn
and will not evade the tax.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל הַמֶּכֶס כּוּלּוֹ שֶׁלְּךָ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the parable begun in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king pays tax to set an example for others.

steps.title: The lesson: ה׳ hates robbery so His children will avoid it
steps.stepSummary: Applying the parable, הקב״ה says He hates robbery in an offering so that His children will learn from Him to stay away from stealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, הקב״ה said: 'I, ה׳, hate robbery in a burnt offering.' My children will learn from Me and keep away from robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the נמשל, the real-life meaning of the parable, applied to ה׳ and the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything in the world belongs to ה׳, so in a sense nothing is stolen 'from' Him. Still, He refuses offerings that come from robbery, to teach His children to avoid stealing altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ rejects stolen offerings not because He needs anything, but to teach us to stay far from stealing.

phrases.english: So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
'I, the Lord, hate robbery in a burnt offering';
from Me My children will learn
and will keep themselves away from robbery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the parable of steps 6–7 to ה׳.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ hates stolen offerings in order to teach His children to avoid robbery.

steps.title: רבי אמי says the same: dry is פסול for lacking beauty, stolen for coming through sin
steps.stepSummary: Supporting רבי יוחנן, רבי אמי rules that a dry לולב is פסול because it lacks הדר, and a stolen לולב is פסול because of מצוה הבאה בעבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי אמי said: a dry one is פסול because it lacks beauty; a stolen one is פסול because it is a מצוה that comes through a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא, רבי אמי, who gives the same reason for a stolen לולב, as support for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אתמר נמי' signals that a separate statement agrees with what came before. רבי אמי also gives two different reasons for two of the משנה's cases. A dry לולב lacks the beauty the Torah requires, while a stolen one is פסול because of the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces supporting evidence)
Beauty, the requirement from 'פרי עץ הדר'

steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate reasons for two separate פסולים: יבש lacks הדר, and גזול is a מצוה הבאה בעבירה.

phrases.english: It was also stated: Rabbi Ami said:
A dry one is unfit
because it lacks beauty;
a stolen one is unfit
because it is
a מצוה that comes through a sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the אגדה to the halachic point, supporting the reasoning of steps 1–5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reason that a stolen לולב is פסול because of מצוה הבאה בעבירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The independent statement of רבי אמי, which gives the same reason.

steps.title: שמואל: a stolen לולב is invalid only on the first day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי אמי disagrees with רבי יצחק בר נחמני, who quotes שמואל. According to שמואל, a stolen לולב is פסול only on the first יום טוב. From the second day on, you are יוצא even with a stolen לולב, just as you are with a borrowed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with רבי יצחק. For רבי יצחק בר נחמני said in the name of שמואל: The rule that a stolen לולב is invalid applies only to the first day of יום טוב. But on the second day, since you can use a borrowed לולב, you can also use a stolen one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different opinion, from שמואל, that clashes with רבי אמי. It shows that רבי אמי's view is not the only view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said a stolen לולב is פסול because of מצוה הבאה בעבירה, and that reason would apply on every day. שמואל instead ties the problem to the word 'לכם' ('your own'), which only applies on the first day. So on later days, a stolen לולב is like a borrowed one, and both work.

keyTerms.meaning: And it argues with (this view disagrees with another)
They only taught this rule in the case of
The second day of the festival (and onward)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמואל allows stealing on the second day. He only says that, after the fact, you are יוצא the מצוה. The theft itself is still forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the two possible reasons a stolen לולב is פסול: 'לכם' (ownership), which is limited to day one, or מצוה הבאה בעבירה, which applies every day.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Yitzchak.
phrases.notes: It's רבי אמי's view from step 9 that argues with what comes next.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ, אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: They only taught this regarding the first day of the festival,
but on the second day of the festival,
since one fulfills the obligation with a borrowed one,
one also fulfills it with a stolen one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי אמי's ruling from step 9 disagrees with שמואל's position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stolen לולב is פסול only on the first day of סוכות. From the second day on, one is יוצא with a stolen לולב, just as with a borrowed one.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: a stolen לולב is invalid even on the second day
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks שמואל from our משנה. The משנה says a stolen or dry לולב is פסול, which implies a borrowed one is כשר. That cannot be the first day, because of 'לכם.' So the משנה must be talking about the second day, and it still says a stolen לולב is פסול. That contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objected: 'A stolen or dry לולב is invalid.' That implies a borrowed one is valid. When is this? If you say on the first day, the Torah says 'לכם,' meaning it must be your own, and a borrowed one is not his. So it must be the second day, and still the משנה says a stolen one is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק uses a careful reading of the משנה to challenge שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1: the משנה lists stolen as פסול but not borrowed, so borrowed must be כשר. Step 2: borrowed cannot be כשר on day one because of 'לכם,' so the משנה must be about later days. Step 3: on those later days the משנה still calls stolen פסול, which goes directly against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies (an inference from what the text says)
'For yourselves' means from your own property

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak raised an objection:
A lulav that is stolen or dry is invalid,
which implies that a borrowed one is valid.
When is this?
If you say on the first day of the festival,
but it is written 'for yourselves,' meaning from your own,
and this one is not his.
Rather, is it not talking about the second day of the festival,
and it teaches that a stolen one is invalid!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that a stolen לולב is כשר from the second day on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies borrowed is כשר. That can only be true after day one, so the משנה must be about later days. Yet it still calls stolen פסול.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה is about the first day, using a 'not only' style
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה really is about the first day. It mentions stolen rather than borrowed because borrowed is obviously פסול, since it is not his. With stolen, you might think יאוש בעלים makes it like his own, so the משנה needed to teach that even stolen is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, the משנה is about the first day, and it speaks in a 'it goes without saying' style. It goes without saying that a borrowed one is invalid, since it is not his. But a stolen one, you might say that in ordinary theft the owner gives up hope, so it counts as the thief's own. The משנה teaches us that it is still invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends שמואל by rereading the משנה so that it is about the first day only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on the inference that borrowed is כשר. רבא removes that inference: the משנה skipped borrowed because it is too obvious, not because it is כשר. Stolen is the bigger חידוש, because יאוש might seem to give the thief ownership. So the משנה fits day one, and שמואל stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes without saying (style: the obvious case is skipped, the new case is stated)
The owner's giving up hope of getting the item back
It is considered like his own

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל as defended by רבא, the problem with a stolen לולב is 'לכם,' and that applies only on the first day. The משנה mentions stolen because it is the less obvious case.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Actually, it is about the first day of the festival,
and it is speaking in an 'it goes without saying' style:
It goes without saying that a borrowed one is invalid,
since it is not his,
but a stolen one, I might say:
ordinary theft involves the owner giving up hope,
and so it is considered like his own,
so the Mishnah teaches us that it is still invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן, וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's style ('לא מיבעיא') to cancel the inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's silence about borrowed means borrowed is כשר, so the משנה must be about the second day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about the first day. Borrowed is obviously פסול, and stolen is mentioned because יאוש might have made it count as his own.

steps.title: רב הונא's advice: let the gentiles cut the myrtle
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the theme of stolen ארבעה מינים, the גמרא brings רב הונא's practical instruction to הדס merchants. When buying הדסים from גוים, the merchants should not cut the branches themselves. The גוים should cut them and then hand them over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to the merchants: When you buy הדסים from גוים, do not cut them yourselves. Let them cut the branches and give them to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from theory to a practical case connected to stolen מינים: how merchants should buy הדסים from גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא worries that the land the הדסים grow on may be stolen. Who does the cutting makes a difference to whether the branches count as stolen for the buyer. The reason is given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Merchants (here, sellers of the ארבעה מינים)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא לְהָנְהוּ אֲוַונְכָּרֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said to those merchants:
When you buy myrtle from gentiles,
do not cut it yourselves,
rather, let them cut it and give it to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא לְהָנְהוּ אֲוַונְכָּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical ruling related to stolen ארבעה מינים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Merchants buying הדסים from גוים should have the גוים cut the branches, not cut them themselves.

steps.title: The reason: gentiles often seize land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב הונא gave this advice. It answers that ordinary גוים are 'land robbers.' The fields the הדסים grow on may have been taken from Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because ordinary גוים are land robbers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב הונא's advice and starts to answer it. The explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that the field was seized from its rightful owner, so the הדס may be stolen property. Land cannot truly be acquired through theft, so it still belongs to the original owner. The גמרא will go on to explain how having the גוי cut the branches solves this problem.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a statement that every individual גוי is a thief. It is a practical assumption about the typical situation then: fields were often seized by force.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Ordinary gentiles are land robbers,
phrases.notes: The explanation continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב הונא's advice in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The land the הדסים grow on is likely stolen, so the merchants must avoid acquiring stolen הדסים.
